requestedActions.title: Read titles and content of pages customers share with the app
Customers authorize the app to connect their workspace via OAuth

guide.summary: Customer-by-customer OAuth integration fits: each customer authorizes the app and selects pages via the page picker, and the app reads titles and content with an access token tied to that user. Installation scope must allow other customer workspaces, so a public integration is required; scoped-to-selected-workspaces integrations cannot serve other organizations. The documented capability needed for reading page content is Read content, which covers retrieving pages and their markdown/block content without insert or update rights. Provider review and marketplace listing are separate from authorization and are not required to start authorization.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read titles and content of pages customers share with the app. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization flow is documented for user-authorized integrations
findings.detail: Each user visits the authorization URL, selects pages via the page picker, and the app exchanges the returned code at the token endpoint for an access token used on behalf of that user. Only that user can interact with the connection in their workspace, so each customer user must authorize individually.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer user connects their own account and shares pages with the app.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading page titles and content
findings.detail: Read content lets the connection read existing content, including retrieving pages and their markdown content; calls fail with 403 without read content capability. Page-level sharing by the customer still limits which pages are visible.
findings.appliesWhen: App reads titles and content of shared pages; read-only.

​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.title: Client credentials and redirect URI must be configured before first test
findings.detail: The OAuth client ID, client secret and redirect URI come from the connection configuration and the Developer portal; the token exchange uses HTTP Basic authentication with those credentials. Authorization can start once client credentials and redirect URI are set; Marketplace submission or review is not required.

evidence.quote: Both scoped OAuth integrations and public integrations use this flow. You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration’s client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review

CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET Find both of these values in the Developer portal .

findings.title: Customer must share pages with the connection through the page picker
findings.detail: Users choose pages in the page picker, which shows only pages they have full access to; the connection can read only the shared pages and their children. Notion does not grant access to unshared pages.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer wants the app to read specific pages.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration in the Developer portal
steps.detail: Open the Developer portal, go to Build > Connections, and create a new connection with Any workspace installation scope so other customer workspaces can install it. Add the redirect URI. Installation scope cannot be changed later.
steps.doneWhen: Connection exists with public installation scope, a redirect URI configured, and OAuth client ID and secret visible in the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Send a test customer through the consent redirect and verify the callback
steps.detail: Visit the authorization URL from the Configuration tab in a test customer account, select pages in the page picker, and approve. Confirm the browser returns to the redirect URI with a code query parameter. Do not exchange the code yet.
steps.doneWhen: Callback URL contains a code parameter and the state value matches the one sent.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Send the code from the callback to the token endpoint using HTTP Basic auth with CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET and a JSON body. Expected output includes access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, workspace_id and owner. Store the token pair per customer.
steps.doneWhen: Response contains access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace_id.

steps.title: Read a shared page's properties and title
steps.detail: Using the access token, retrieve a page the customer shared. The response is a page object; the title is found in properties by the property whose type is title, typically the key named Name or title. Expected output is a page object with an id and object equal to page.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with object equal to page and the title property present. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
